title: Twelve guarded hours
subtitle: Every division of the night is a door with a name on it
question: What kind of knowledge does an Underworld Book claim to give, and to whom?
place: Royal tombs, Valley of the Kings
evidenceBoundary: The Duat is not one fixed map. The Amduat and the Book of Gates divide the night differently and disagree about what matters at each stage. The course packets for both are mainly image plates with very little extractable prose; the Budge translations that accompany them are over a century old. Hour titles below follow the structure the packets show rather than a modern critical edition.
reconstruction: This walkthrough presents the shared structure the wiki sets out, then marks where the two compositions diverge. Where the archive records only images, the scene says so.
accessibleSummary: Twelve numbered stages in a table, each with the composition it belongs to, what guards it, and what changes.

scenes.title: Hour 1 — entering the west
scenes.body: Re passes the western horizon and the bark enters a different order of space. The living world's rules stop applying at this line.
detail: The tomb itself is built to be this environment.

scenes.title: Hours 2 and 3 — the watery regions
scenes.body: Wide waters and fields. The bark travels in a middle register with populations above and below: gods, blessed dead, and the inert.
detail: The register layout is the argument. Position on the page is position in the cosmos.

scenes.title: Hours 4 and 5 — the difficult ground
scenes.body: The route becomes sand, caves, and closed passages. The bark has to be dragged. Sokar's region belongs here, deep underground and associated with regeneration in darkness.
detail: Movement stops being automatic and becomes work.

scenes.title: Hour 6 — the union
scenes.body: The solar ba unites with the Osirian body at the deepest point of the night. This is the turning point of the whole composition.
detail: Mobility and preserved body meet. Neither achieves renewal alone.

scenes.title: Hours 7 to 9 — Apep
scenes.body: The serpent is bound, cut, and turned back. Enemies are restrained and, in the Book of Gates, punished with fire. Non-order is handled, not abolished.
detail: The same operation will be needed tomorrow night.

scenes.title: The gates
scenes.body: Great serpents and gate-lines divide the route repeatedly. Named keepers guard each transition, so every threshold becomes a problem of knowledge and authorisation rather than of strength.
detail: Knowing the name is the pass.
This is why the composition is written on the walls of the tomb of someone who will need to make the journey.

scenes.title: The hall of Osiris
scenes.body: The Book of Gates includes a judgment hall with Osiris enthroned, and a famous scene grouping the peoples known to Egypt. The sun's ordered cosmos extends past Egyptians, described in Egyptian ethnographic categories.
detail: This scene is regularly quoted out of context. Its frame is the solar circuit, not a statement of equality.

scenes.title: Hour 12 — emergence
scenes.body: Beings pass through the body of a great serpent and come out renewed. The sun emerges as Khepri. The Book of Gates closes by composing Nun, Nut, bark, and scarab into a single rebirth image.
detail: Passing through the serpent is a visual grammar for renewal, not a narrative event to be literalised.
